title: Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Announces Inducement Grant Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
summary: SAN DIEGO, May 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - Zentalis ® Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZNTL), a clinical oncology innovator advancing late-stage development of investigational first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor azenosertib as a biomarker-driven treatment approach for ovarian cancer, today announced that on May 1, 2026, the Compensation Committee of Zentalis’ Board of Directors granted non-qualified stock options to purchase an aggregate of 26,000 shares of the Company’s common stock to one (1) newly hired employee. The stock options were granted under the Zentalis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 2022 Employment Inducement Incentive Award Plan (2022 Inducement Plan) as an inducement material to such individual’s entering into employment with Zentalis in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The 2022 Inducement Plan is used exclusively for the grant of equity awards to individuals who were not previously employees of Zentalis, or following a bona fide period of non-employment, as an inducement
body_text: View All News Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Announces Inducement Grant Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4) May 1, 2026 Download (opens in new window) SAN DIEGO, May 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Zentalis® Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZNTL), a clinical oncology innovator advancing late-stage development of investigational first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor azenosertib as a biomarker-driven treatment approach for ovarian cancer, today announced that on May 1, 2026, the Compensation Committee of Zentalis’ Board of Directors granted non-qualified stock options to purchase an aggregate of 26,000 shares of the Company’s common stock to one (1) newly hired employee. The stock options were granted under the Zentalis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. 2022 Employment Inducement Incentive Award Plan (2022 Inducement Plan) as an inducement material to such individual’s entering into employment with Zentalis in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The 2022 Inducement Plan is used exclusively for the grant of equity awards to individuals who were not previously employees of Zentalis, or following a bona fide period of non-employment, as an inducement material to each such individual’s entering into employment with Zentalis, pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The stock options have an exercise price of $4.09 per share, which is equal to the closing price of Zentalis’ common stock on The Nasdaq Global Market on the date of grant. The stock options have a 10-year term and will vest over four years, with 25% of the options vesting on the first anniversary of the vesting commencement date and the remaining 75% of the options vesting in equal monthly installments over the three years thereafter. Vesting of the stock options is subject to the employee’s continued service to Zentalis on each vesting date. About Zentalis Pharmaceuticals Zentalis is a clinical oncology innovator developing a treatment approach for ovarian cancer and multiple tumor types. Leveraging therapeutics development and biomarker expertise, Zentalis is advancing monotherapy and combination studies of its first-in-class WEE1 inhibitor, azenosertib. Focused on translating WEE1 science into clinical practice, we aim to equip physicians with a targeted, non-chemo, orally available medicine that enhances treatment experience, choice, and outcomes. Our mission: to unburden cancer patients with more convenience and care.​ For more information, please visit www.zentalis.com . Follow Zentalis on LinkedIn at www.linkedin.com/company/zentalis-pharmaceuticals . ZENTALIS ® and its associated logo are trademarks of Zentalis and/or its affiliates. title: Smackover Lithium Announces the Award of Well Field EPCM Contract for the South West Arkansas Project Ahead of Final Investment Decision
summary: Standard Lithium is a leading near-commercial lithium company focused on the sustainable development of a portfolio of large, high-grade lithium-brine properties in the United States.
body_text: Smackover Lithium Announces the Award of Well Field EPCM Contract for the South West Arkansas Project Ahead of Final Investment Decision May 21, 2026 Download PDF All figures are in US dollars unless otherwise stated. LEWISVILLE, Ark., May 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Smackover Lithium, a partnership between Standard Lithium Ltd. (“Standard Lithium” or the “Company”) (TSXV: SLI) (NYSE.A: SLI) and Equinor, through subsidiaries of Equinor ASA, announced that it has entered into an engineering, procurement, and construction management (“EPCM”) agreement (the “Agreement”) with Wood Group USA, Inc. (“Wood”) focused on the upstream well field portion of the South West Arkansas Project (“SWA Project” or the “Project”). Wood is a global leader in consulting, engineering and operations for the energy and materials sectors and has significant expertise in managing complex, multi-disciplinary projects encompassing EPCM across diverse sectors, including lithium and broader minerals. The well field for the SWA Project comprises four (4) well pads supporting twelve (12) supply and ten (10) injection wells, brine gathering and return pipelines from the well pads to the Central Processing Facility (“CPF”), and a gas gathering system from the well pads to a disposal well in the area. Wood will deliver EPCM services for the well field surface facilities including well pads, pipelines, and related third-party interfaces. The scope includes Project support services for the subsurface, drilling and wells activities, which will be led by the Project team, leveraging Equinor’s strong internal expertise and capabilities. A separate engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (“EPCC”) agreement is expected to be signed with a different counterparty for the CPF, which includes the direct lithium extraction process and conversion to battery-quality lithium carbonate. The EPCC agreement is also expected to be completed in the second quarter. The SWA Project is designed to produce 22,500 tonnes per annum of battery-quality lithium carbonate production in its initial phase. Upstream well field-related activities account for less than one-third of the Project’s estimated capital expenditure, the latest published details of which are provided in the Definitive Feasibility Study filed on October 15th, 2025. The Agreement includes a Limited Notice to Proceed (“LNTP”) that allows work to continue on key activities to de-risk the Project and optimize the construction schedule. Under the LNTP, work will focus on detailed engineering, advancing permitting and early procurement activities related to identifying and engaging contractors and vendors of major equipment and materials. The expectation is to engage Wood on a Full Notice to Proceed following a positive Final Investment Decision, which is expected to occur in 2026. Dr. Andy Robinson, President and COO of Standard Lithium stated, “We are excited by the opportunity to work with Wood and value the experience and reliability they bring to our Project. Signing this Agreement was made possible by our 18-month detailed front-end engineering design (FEED) process that yielded strong capital definition and is critical as we prepare for a Final Investment Decision before moving into construction shortly thereafter.” "We are pleased to partner with Smackover Lithium on the development of this important Project," said Richard Neale, Regional President, Americas at Wood. “Battery-quality lithium carbonate is critical to strengthening the United States domestic supply chain and this Project marks a meaningful step towards securing critical minerals. We have been impressed by the Project’s technical foundation and front-end design work and we look forward to applying our predictable and proven delivery expertise to the Project to help execute safely and successfully, whilst supporting a more resilient minerals supply chain.” The Definitive Feasibility Study for the SWA Project is available for review under the Company’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the Company’s website at https://www.standardlithium.com/projects/smackover/south-west-arkansas/ . For highlights of this study, please refer to the Company’s press release dated 3 September 2025 . Department of Energy Acknowledgement and Disclaimer This material is based upon work supported by the U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation under award Number DE-MS0000099. The views expressed herein do not necessarily represent the views of the U.S. Department of Energy or the United States Government. About Smackover Lithium Smackover Lithium is a partnership between Standard Lithium and Equinor, through subsidiaries of Equinor ASA. Formed in May 2024, Smackover Lithium is developing multiple direct lithium extraction (“DLE”) projects in Southwest Arkansas and East Texas. Standard Lithium owns a 55% interest and Equinor holds the remaining 45% interest in the projects, with Standard Lithium maintaining operatorship. About Standard Lithium Ltd. Standard Lithium is a leading near-commercial lithium development company focused on the sustainable development of a portfolio of large, high-grade lithium-brine properties in the United States. The Company prioritizes projects characterized by high-grade resources, robust infrastructure, skilled labor, and streamlined permitting. Standard Lithium aims to achieve sustainable, commercial-scale lithium production via the application of a scalable and fully integrated DLE and purification process. The Company’s flagship projects are in the Smackover Formation, a world-class lithium brine asset, focused in Arkansas and Texas. In partnership with global energy leader Equinor, Standard Lithium is advancing the SWA Project, a greenfield project located in southern Arkansas, and actively advancing a promising lithium brine resource position in East Texas, including the highest known lithium brine grade project in North America, the Franklin Project. Standard Lithium trades on both the TSX Venture Exchange (“TSXV”) and the NYSE American under the symbol “SLI”. Visit the Company’s website at www.standardlithium.com for more information. About Equinor Equinor is an international energy company committed to long-term value creation in a low-carbon future. Equinor’s portfolio of projects encompasses oil and gas, renewables, and low-carbon solutions, with an ambition of becoming a net-zero energy company by 2050. Headquartered in Norway, Equinor is the leading operator on the Norwegian continental shelf and has offices in more than 20 countries worldwide. Equinor’s partnership with Standard Lithium to mature DLE projects builds on its broad US energy portfolio of oil and gas, offshore wind, low carbon solutions, and battery storage projects. For more information on Equinor in the U.S., please visit: Equinor in the US - Equinor . About Wood Wood is a global leader in consulting, engineering and operations for the energy and materials sectors. With 33,000 people in around 50 countries, Wood supports clients across the full asset lifecycle, delivering safe, predictable outcomes while enabling resilient operations and a lower-carbon future. Wood forms the Energy & Materials pillar of Sidara - a global partnership uniting leading multidisciplinary engineering, design, and project management companies. www.woodgroup.com . title: Guide to Homeowners Insurance in Riverside, CA [2026]
summary: Guide to homeowners insurance in Riverside, CA for 2026. Learn about Riverside homeowners insurance cost, coverage options, and how to get homeowners insurance in Riverside despite market volatility.
body_text: Guide to Homeowners Insurance in Riverside, CA [2026] Riverside sits at the heart of the Inland Empire, where Mediterranean climate meets the foothills of the San Bernardino Mountains. That geography creates both appeal and insurance complexity. The city's wildfire exposure, combined with California's broader market turmoil, has pushed premiums higher and made carrier availability less predictable than homeowners might expect. This guide breaks down what homeowners insurance costs in Riverside right now, what standard policies cover and exclude, and how to shop for coverage without leaving gaps that could cost thousands after a claim. What does homeowners insurance cost in Riverside? Riverside premiums tend to run above the California typical because of the city's inland location and proximity to fire-prone terrain. Coverage Cat's internal home pricing data from September 27, 2023 through June 8, 2026 shows the following snapshot: Geography Typical quoted annual range Typical quoted 10th-percentile range Typical quoted 90th-percentile range California statewide $2,000-$2,400 $950-$1,000 $4,300-$4,400 Riverside $2,000-$2,400 — — That $2,000-$2,400 range reflects the typical quoted premium in Coverage Cat's Riverside quote flow. It should not be read as a public market average because it captures only homeowners who sought quotes through Coverage Cat, not the broader market. Still, it signals that Riverside tends to land above the statewide typical. Coverage Cat's recent weighted California pricing data for the recent weighted market window suggests many lowest annual quotes in Riverside land around roughly $2,000-$2,400 with higher-risk properties or older roofs pushing well above $3,000-$3,100. Public pricing comparison Finding city-specific premium benchmarks for Riverside proves difficult because most public sources report only statewide or regional averages. The California Department of Insurance publishes rate filings but does not release granular city-level premium surveys. For high-risk California zones with dwelling coverage around $500,000, Insurance Journal reports annual premiums often land between $3,500 and $5,000 (Insurance Journal, "Homeowners in CA high-risk zones", 2026) . Riverside's wildfire-adjacent neighborhoods likely fall into this range, while lower-risk areas closer to the city center may see premiums closer to the $2,000–$2,500 band. Source Coverage Area Annual Premium Signal Coverage Cat (internal) Riverside $2,000-$2,400 for many lowest quotes Coverage Cat (internal) California statewide $1,900-$2,300 for many lowest quotes MoneyGeek California statewide ~$2,500-$2,600 average (2025) Insurance Journal CA high-risk zones ($500-$550K dwelling) $3,500-$5,250 Treat these figures as directional context rather than binding estimates. Your actual premium depends on your home's location, rebuild cost, roof condition, claims history, and chosen coverage limits. What does homeowners insurance cover (and what it usually excludes)? A standard HO-3 policy provides six coverage categories. Understanding each helps you spot gaps before they become expensive surprises. Dwelling coverage (Coverage A) pays to repair or rebuild your home's structure after covered perils like fire, windstorm, hail, or vandalism. In Riverside, where rebuild costs have climbed alongside labor and material prices, adequate dwelling limits matter more than ever. Other structures (Coverage B) covers detached garages, sheds, fences, and pools. Most policies set this at 10% of your dwelling limit by default. Personal property (Coverage C) reimburses you for belongings damaged or stolen. Standard policies use actual cash value, which deducts depreciation. Replacement cost coverage, available as an endorsement, pays what it costs to replace items at current prices. Loss of use (Coverage D) covers additional living expenses if you cannot occupy your home during repairs. This includes hotel stays, restaurant meals above your normal food budget, and temporary rentals. Personal liability (Coverage E) protects you if someone sues after an injury on your property or if you damage someone else's property. Standard limits start at $100,000, but most financial planners recommend at least $300,000. Medical payments (Coverage F) pays small medical bills for guests injured on your property regardless of fault, typically capped at $1,000–$5,000. Common exclusions Every HO-3 policy excludes certain perils. In Riverside, these exclusions carry particular weight: Earthquake damage requires a separate policy or endorsement. Given Southern California's seismic activity, many Riverside homeowners purchase coverage through the California Earthquake Authority or private carriers. Flood damage falls outside standard homeowners policies. Homes near the Santa Ana River or in low-lying areas may need a separate flood policy through FEMA's National Flood Insurance Program or a private flood insurer. Earth movement beyond earthquakes, including landslide and mudflow, is typically excluded. Some policies offer limited mudflow coverage after a wildfire denudes slopes. Wear and tear and maintenance failures are never covered. If your roof leaks because you neglected repairs, the resulting water damage falls on you. Certain wildfire or smoke limitations appear in some California policies. Carriers may impose sub-limits on smoke damage or exclude coverage for homes that fail to meet defensible space requirements. Review your policy's fire provisions carefully because California home premiums keep rising in part due to wildfire losses. Why California pricing and availability can be volatile (and what Riverside homeowners can do) California's homeowners insurance market has experienced sustained disruption since 2020. Multiple carriers have paused new business, reduced capacity, or exited entirely. The reasons interconnect: rising wildfire losses, reinsurance costs that jumped after global catastrophe events, and regulatory constraints that limited rate adjustments. Deloitte's 2026 insurance outlook notes that P&C premium growth has declined to below 4% nationally, but margin pressure from catastrophe events continues to shape pricing in exposed states like California (Deloitte Insights, "Insurance Industry Outlook", 2026) . Markel's trend analysis expects 3–4% premium growth nationally with continued discipline on fire-prone risks (Markel, "Top 10 Insurance Trends for 2026", 2026) . For Riverside specifically, the Inland Empire's proximity to wildfire-prone canyons and the recent expansion of the wildland-urban interface have made underwriting tighter. Some national carriers that once wrote freely in the area now decline new applications or require extensive documentation. What Riverside homeowners can do Create defensible space. Cal Fire requires 100 feet of defensible space around structures in fire-prone areas. Clearing brush, trimming trees, and removing dead vegetation not only reduces fire risk but also improves your insurability. Some carriers now use aerial imagery to verify compliance before issuing policies. Upgrade your roof. Roof age and material affect both premiums and availability. Class A fire-rated roofing, including concrete tile, metal, and certain asphalt shingles, can qualify for discounts. A roof over 20 years old may trigger surcharges or non-renewal. Harden your home. Enclosed eaves, ember-resistant vents, and tempered glass windows reduce fire vulnerability. California's Wildfire Preparedness program offers guidance on home hardening measures that some insurers recognize with premium credits. Document everything. Keep records of permits, inspections, and receipts for upgrades. When you apply for coverage or renew, detailed documentation helps underwriters assess your home accurately and may prevent coverage denials. Know your fallback options. If admitted carriers decline coverage, companies still insuring homes in California include surplus lines carriers and specialty insurers. The California FAIR Plan exists as a last resort for homes that cannot find coverage elsewhere, though its premiums tend to run higher and its coverage more limited than standard policies. For more on navigating these options, see Coverage Cat's guide to finding insurance in high-risk wildfire zones . Riverside homeowners should budget for possible increases and explore mitigation credits wherever available. How to choose limits and endorsements so you are not underinsured Underinsurance remains one of the most common problems after major losses. Homeowners who set dwelling limits based on their mortgage balance or purchase price often discover those figures fall far short of actual rebuild costs. Rebuild cost versus market value Your home's market value includes land, location desirability, and neighborhood comparables. Rebuild cost reflects only what it would take to reconstruct the structure from the ground up, including materials, labor, permits, and debris removal. In Riverside, where labor shortages have driven construction costs higher, rebuild costs often exceed market value for older homes in established neighborhoods. Request a replacement cost estimate from your insurer or hire an independent appraiser. Do not rely on Zillow estimates or tax assessments because neither reflects actual rebuild costs. Endorsements worth considering Standard HO-3 policies leave gaps that endorsements can fill. Coverage Cat's guide to which homeowners endorsements are worth the money covers this in detail, but here are the most relevant for Riverside: Extended replacement cost adds a buffer, typically 25–50%, above your dwelling limit. If a widespread disaster drives up contractor demand and material prices, this buffer helps ensure you can still rebuild. Ordinance or law coverage pays for upgrades required by current building codes. Older Riverside homes built before modern fire codes may need significant upgrades after a partial loss. Without this endorsement, you pay the difference out of pocket. Water backup coverage protects against sewer or drain backups, which standard policies exclude. This endorsement typically costs $20–$50 annually and covers a common claim type. Higher personal liability limits make sense for homeowners with significant assets to protect. Increasing from $100,000 to $500,000 in liability coverage often costs less than $50 per year. Homeowners with pools, dogs, or frequent guests should consider umbrella policies for additional protection. Scheduled personal property provides agreed-value coverage for high-value items like jewelry, art, or collectibles. Standard personal property limits often cap specific categories at $1,500–$2,500, which may not cover a single engagement ring. How to shop for homeowners insurance in Riverside Finding coverage in Riverside requires more effort than in lower-risk markets. Follow this step-by-step process to get accurate quotes and compare policies properly. Step 1: Gather your documentation Before requesting quotes, compile: Your home's square footage, year built, and construction type Roof material and age (or date of last replacement) Recent upgrades with permits and receipts Photos showing defensible space compliance Your claims history for the past five years Current insurance declarations page if you have existing coverage Step 2: Determine your coverage needs Calculate your dwelling coverage requirement using a rebuild cost estimator or professional appraisal. Set personal property limits based on a home inventory. Choose liability limits based on your net worth and risk exposure. Step 3: Request quotes from multiple sources Coverage Cat's quote flow often surfaces specialty carriers such as Lightspeed, Delos, Bamboo, Homesite, and Obie, which commonly write in California's tighter market. An independent broker with access to multiple carriers can also help you compare options. For a broader view of what's available, see Coverage Cat's best California homeowners insurance carriers ranked . Step 4: Compare policy forms, not just price A $1,800-$1,900 policy that excludes water damage coverage is not equivalent to a $2,100-$2,200 policy that includes it. When comparing quotes, examine: Coverage limits for each section (A through F) Deductibles, including any separate fire or wind deductibles Exclusions and limitations specific to each policy Endorsements included or available Claims payment reputation (check California Department of Insurance complaint ratios) Step 5: Ask about discounts Common discounts include: Bundling home and auto policies (typically 5–15% off) New roof or fire-resistant roofing (varies by carrier) Home security systems and smoke detectors Claims-free history Paying annually instead of monthly Step 6: Work with a specialist broker if needed If standard carriers decline your application, a surplus lines broker can access non-admitted carriers that write higher-risk properties. These policies may cost more and offer different terms, but they provide coverage when standard markets will not. Coverage Cat's guide to regional availability of California home insurance explains how availability varies by location. Shopping Step What to Do Why It Matters Documentation Gather photos, permits, roof age Speeds underwriting, may prevent declines Coverage calculation Use rebuild cost estimator Avoids underinsurance at claim time Multiple quotes Get 3–5 quotes minimum Prices vary widely across carriers Policy comparison Read exclusions and forms Cheapest price may have worst coverage Discount check Ask about bundling, roof, claims-free Can save 10–20% on premium Specialist broker Use if declined by standard carriers Access to surplus lines market Summary Riverside homeowners face a market that demands more attention than it did five years ago. Premiums have risen, carrier availability has tightened, and wildfire exposure adds complexity that other California cities do not share. The shopping checklist: gather documentation before you quote, calculate rebuild cost rather than market value, request quotes from at least three to five sources, and compare coverage terms rather than price alone. If standard carriers decline, a surplus lines broker can access specialty markets. Use both Coverage Cat's internal pricing signals, which show many Riverside quotes landing around $2,000-$2,400 and public benchmarks like Insurance Journal's $3,500-$5,250 range for high-risk zones as directional context. Your actual premium depends on your specific property, risk profile, and coverage choices. Take time to review endorsements. Extended replacement cost, ordinance or law coverage, and water backup protection cost relatively little but close gaps that could otherwise cost thousands. Document your home's condition, maintain defensible space, and keep records of upgrades because these steps improve both your insurability and your claim outcomes if the worst happens. FAQs About Homeowners Insurance in Riverside, CA How much dwelling coverage do I need in Riverside? Dwelling coverage should track rebuild cost, not the home's market value. Use a replacement-cost estimator and update it after renovations or major price changes in labor and materials. What is an HO-3 policy and why is it common? HO-3 is the most common homeowners policy form. It typically covers the dwelling on an open-perils basis (covered unless excluded) while personal property is usually named-perils. What does homeowners insurance usually not cover? Flooding and earthquakes usually require separate policies. Wear and tear, maintenance issues, and many earth-movement losses are also commonly excluded. When should I consider an umbrella policy? If you have meaningful assets or higher liability exposure, an umbrella policy can add extra protection above your home and auto liability limits. How do I shop for coverage if my home is in a wildfire-risk area? Start early, be ready to provide detailed property information, and compare private-market options against FAIR Plan plus a companion policy when necessary.

Conductor: Deterministic orchestration for multi-agent AI workflows
summary: Conductor is an open-source CLI (MIT license, Microsoft org) that takes a different approach: you define your multi-agent workflows in YAML, and the routing between agents is deterministic.
body_text: Multi-agent AI systems are becoming the default approach for complex tasks: Code review pipelines. Research-then-synthesize workflows. Plan-then-implement loops. These aren’t single-prompt problems. They need multiple specialized agents coordinating in sequence, in parallel, and sometimes in cycles. Most frameworks approach this by making the orchestrator itself an LLM—an agent that dynamically plans which agents to call, in what order, and with what inputs. That works when the task is exploratory. But for workflows with known structure (and in practice, many of the most useful workflows do have known structure), dynamic orchestration adds cost, latency, and unpredictability that can work against you. Conductor is an open-source CLI (MIT license, Microsoft org) that takes a different approach: you define your multi-agent workflows in YAML, and the routing between agents is deterministic. Jinja2 templates and expression evaluation handle conditions and branching. The orchestration layer consumes zero tokens. The structure is fixed at definition time—and that’s the point. Dig into Conductor today The problem with multi-agent workflows today We kept building multi-agent workflows—code review pipelines, design document generation, research assistants—and writing the same glue code every time: Python scripts stitching prompt chains, ad hoc retries, manual state between steps, no good way to version-control the workflow itself. We looked at other tools, such as Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF), Microsoft’s primary SDK for building agents in code, which covers many of the same primitives. Conductor is a different surface for similar patterns: a YAML-first CLI for teams who want to compose agents and tools without writing SDK code. Declared, diffable, and as readable as a CI/CD pipeline. We also wanted to separate concerns that keep getting mashed together in multi-agent systems: Orchestration should be deterministic and inspectable. Not an LLM making routing decisions. Execution should support multiple providers and models, so you can put a cheap model on triage and a capable one on reasoning. Context flow between agents should be explicit. No implicit conversation bleeding. Human oversight should be a built-in workflow step, not something you bolt on later. Conductor is the result : YAML workflows, isolated agents, and a routing graph you can see before anything runs. Key capabilities of Conductor YAML-defined workflows Every Conductor workflow is a YAML file that declares agents, their prompts, models, inputs, outputs, and routing logic. Workflows are version-controlled, diffable, and reviewable, the same way you’d treat infrastructure-as-code or CI/CD pipelines. workflow: name: design-review entry_point: architect agents: - name: architect model: claude-opus-4.6-1m prompt: | Create a design document for: {{ workflow.input.purpose }} output: file_path: { type: string } routes: - to: reviewer - name: reviewer model: claude-opus-4.7 prompt: | Review the design at {{ architect.output.file_path }} output: score: { type: number } approved: { type: boolean } routes: - to: $end when: "{{ output.approved }}" - to: architect Deterministic routing, zero token overhead Routing between agents uses Jinja2 templates and expression evaluation. First matching condition wins. A workflow can loop hundreds of times through an evaluator-optimizer cycle without the routing layer consuming any tokens. This is what separates Conductor from dynamic orchestration: the workflow topology is declared, not discovered at runtime. Mix providers and models per agent Conductor supports GitHub Copilot and Anthropic Claude as providers, with per-agent model overrides. You can mix them in a single workflow: run claude-haiku-4.5 for classification, gpt-5.2 for research with MCP tool access, and claude-opus-4.6-1m for complex reasoning. Each agent gets its own session with no shared conversation state. Parallel execution Static parallel groups run multiple agents concurrently with configurable failure modes (fail_fast, continue_on_error, all_or_nothing). Dynamic for each groups process variable-length arrays in parallel with batched concurrency. Results are aggregated and available to downstream agents through template expressions. parallel: - name: researchers agents: [academic, web, technical] failure_mode: continue_on_error routes: -to:synthesizer Script steps Not every step needs an LLM. Script steps run shell commands directly, capturing stdout, stderr, and exit codes into the workflow context. A code review workflow can run pytest between the “implement” and “review” steps. Routes can branch on exit codes. No model invocation, no token cost. Human gates Human gate steps pause execution, present options in a Rich terminal UI or the web dashboard, and route based on the response. Approval workflows, review checkpoints, interactive decision points: they’re part of the workflow graph, defined the same way as any other step. Web dashboard Conductor includes a web dashboard that visualizes execution in real time. An interactive DAG shows the workflow topology with animated edges for execution flow. Each node is clickable, showing the agent’s prompt, model, token usage, cost, activity stream, and output. Human gates work directly in the browser. Background mode (–web-bg) starts the dashboard, prints the URL, and returns control to the terminal. Context control Three context modes control what each agent sees: accumulate (all prior outputs), last_only (just the previous step), and explicit (only named dependencies). The default is accumulated, but for larger workflows, explicit mode cuts token consumption significantly. Being deliberate about what each agent sees turned out to matter more than we expected. Plugins and workflow registries Plugins follow the Agent Skills open standard, bundling reusable skills and MCP server configurations that agents can use. Reference them from Git repos or local paths. Workflow registries let teams share and version workflows: configure a registry once, then run workflows by short name. Safety limits Max iteration limits and wall-clock timeouts prevent runaway execution. Dry-run mode previews the execution plan without calling any models. conductor validate catches schema errors, missing references, and unreachable agents before anything runs. Works with your existing tools Conductor doesn’t replace your editor, CI system, or agent framework. It’s a CLI that reads YAML, calls models, and produces structured output. It plugs into what you already have: MCP servers give agents tool access: web search, documentation lookup, code analysis, anything with a Model Context Protocol server. Shell commands run directly as workflow steps, so your scripts, linters, test suites, and build tools participate without modification. Structured output with JSON schemas means downstream tools and scripts can consume results programmatically. A Claude skill ships in the repository. Point your coding agent at it and it can build workflows for you. What we learned 1. Determinism is a feature The most common pushback is “what about dynamic orchestration?” Fair question. If your task needs to restructure itself based on what it discovers, let the LLM decide what comes next. But the workflows we keep reaching for (review loops, research pipelines, plan-then-implement) have known structure. We’d rather have predictability, cost control, and auditability than replanning flexibility. Conditional routing and loop-back patterns cover more ground than you’d expect. 2. Agent isolation pays for itself Each agent gets its own session, system prompt, model, provider, and temperature. No shared conversation bleeding. This seems like overhead until you’re debugging a workflow where step 4 is mysteriously influenced by step 2’s output. Explicit context flow makes multi-agent systems tractable. 3. Events over logs The engine uses a pub/sub event system for all output. The terminal renderer, web dashboard, and any future consumers subscribe independently. More work upfront than printing to stdout, but it decoupled the execution engine from the presentation layer in a way that keeps paying off. Adding the web dashboard required zero changes to the workflow engine. 4. YAML is the right level of abstraction We considered Python APIs, JSON schemas, and visual builders. YAML hit the sweet spot: readable, structured, diffable in pull requests, and familiar to anyone who’s written a GitHub Actions workflow or a Kubernetes manifest. Open source and ready to use MIT-licensed, developed in the open from day one. pytest test suite covering the engine, CLI, config validation, providers, and integration scenarios. Ruff for linting and formatting, ty for type checking, both enforced in CI. Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows. One-line installers (curl | sh and irm | iex) with SHA-256 checksum verification. Self-update via conductor update. Contributions welcome: provider integrations, workflow examples, plugins, docs, bug reports. How to start using Conductor today Install: # macOS / Linux curl -sSfL https://aka.ms/conductor/install.sh | sh # Windows (PowerShell) irm https://aka.ms/conductor/install.ps1 | iex Run your first workflow: conductor run workflow.yaml –input question=”What is Python?” Visualize it: conductor run workflow.yaml –web –input topic=”AI in healthcare” Conductor requires Python 3.12+ and works with GitHub Copilot or Anthropic Claude. The repository has documentation, example workflows, and a getting-started guide. Multi-agent workflows are becoming infrastructure: repeatable, versioned, shared across teams. We chose deterministic orchestration because for the workflows we build most often, known structure is the whole point. Start using Conductor If you’re stitching together agent pipelines with glue code, give Conductor a look. Explore more Conductor is open source under the MIT license at github.com/microsoft/conductor .

title: No Fap Benefits: What You Can Expect To Gain
summary: Discover the real NoFap benefits backed by psychology and behavioral science, including improved focus, confidence, discipline, libido, and emotional control after quitting porn.
body_text: Key takeaways about No Fap Benefits NoFap benefits are often caused by quitting compulsive porn use and reducing overstimulation, not by “semen retention superpowers.” Many men report improved focus, motivation, confidence, discipline, and emotional control after removing porn and compulsive masturbation. Porn can condition the brain to chase constant novelty and instant gratification, making normal life feel less stimulating over time. Quitting porn may help restore attention span, emotional resilience, and enjoyment from ordinary activities. NoFap can improve sexual health by reducing dependence on fantasy and increasing attraction to real-world intimacy. Many users experience withdrawal symptoms early on, including cravings, irritability, anxiety, and low motivation. Long-term success usually comes from replacing compulsive behaviors with healthier routines, goals, and relationships. The biggest NoFap benefit for many men is regaining agency, self-respect, and control over their attention and behavior Frequently Asked Questions About NoFap Benefits Are NoFap benefits actually real? Yes, many NoFap benefits are real, especially for people struggling with compulsive porn use. Most reported improvements—such as better focus, motivation, confidence, and emotional control—likely come from reducing overstimulation and regaining control over compulsive behavior rather than from semen retention itself. How long does it take to notice NoFap benefits? Some people notice changes within the first 1–2 weeks, including reduced guilt, better sleep, and increased mental clarity. More substantial benefits like stronger discipline, emotional stability, and improved sexual function often appear between 30–90 days as the brain adjusts to lower levels of stimulation. Does NoFap increase testosterone? Research does not strongly support claims that NoFap causes massive or permanent testosterone increases. While there may be temporary hormonal fluctuations, most long-term NoFap benefits are more likely tied to behavioral changes, improved discipline, and reduced compulsive pornography use. Can NoFap improve erectile dysfunction? For some men, quitting porn may improve porn-induced erectile dysfunction (PIED), delayed ejaculation, and reduced sexual sensitivity. This happens because the brain can gradually recondition itself to respond to real-world intimacy instead of constant digital novelty and overstimulation. What is the biggest benefit of NoFap? The biggest NoFap benefit for many men is regaining agency over their attention, impulses, and behavior. Many users describe improved self-respect, stronger discipline, clearer thinking, and a greater sense of control over their lives after quitting compulsive porn use. Relay is a therapist-backed group recovery program for pornography and unwanted sexual behavior, combining daily accountability, real-time urge support, and a private peer community. No Fap Benefits: What You Can Expect To Gain NoFap benefits are real for many men, but not always for the reasons the internet claims. The real power of NoFap is not that avoiding ejaculation magically turns you into a different person. It’s that quitting porn and compulsive masturbation gives you a chance to take back control of your attention, your dopamine, your discipline, and your self-respect. That’s why men report better focus, more confidence, higher motivation, stronger sexual desire, less shame, and a greater sense of purpose after starting NoFap. Not because semen is some mystical life force. But because porn can become a shortcut that trains your brain to chase pleasure without effort, intimacy without risk, and stimulation without responsibility. NoFap interrupts that cycle. This article breaks down the most commonly reported NoFap benefits, what science can actually support, what is probably exaggerated, and why quitting porn may improve your mind, body, sex life, and discipline over time. What Are the Real Benefits of NoFap? The internet loves to talk about NoFap like it gives men superpowers. You’ll hear claims about: magnetic charisma female attraction testosterone explosions spiritual enlightenment endless energy becoming “alpha” Some of this is exaggerated, but some of it points to something real. When men quit porn and compulsive masturbation , they often experience meaningful psychological and behavioral changes. The mistake is assuming all those changes come directly from semen retention itself. In reality, many NoFap benefits likely come from removing a compulsive behavior that hijacks attention, motivation, and emotional regulation. Porn creates a powerful artificial reward loop. Novelty. Anticipation. Dopamine spikes. Instant gratification. Repeat. Over time, your brain adapts to that stimulation. What once felt exciting becomes normal. More novelty is needed to produce the same effect. Your attention span shortens while, simultaneously, your tolerance increases. Real life starts to feel slower and less stimulating by comparison. That’s why many men don’t just describe porn as a habit. They describe feeling trapped by it. NoFap benefits often begin when that cycle is interrupted. Instead of constantly chasing stimulation, your brain slowly relearns how to tolerate boredom, delay gratification, focus deeply, and enjoy ordinary experiences again. That’s why many men report: clearer thinking improved focus reduced anxiety more motivation better emotional control stronger confidence healthier sexual desire less compulsive behavior These benefits are not some magic of semen retention. They’re what happens when your mind stops constantly pulling itself toward easy dopamine. And for many men, that change affects every area of life. Porn Changes More Than Your Sex Drive One of the biggest misunderstandings about porn addiction is thinking the damage is purely sexual. For many men, the real damage is psychological. Porn doesn’t just affect arousal. It eradicates attention, destroys motivation, eviscerates emotional regulation, and wipes out impulse control. You're no longer able to tolerate discomfort, and discomfort often accompanies many things, including things we want to do. So, naturally, you stop doing them. And then a downward spiral begins because your brain learns from repetition. Every time you feel: stressed lonely anxious bored rejected overwhelmed …and immediately escape into porn, your brain strengthens that pathway. You stop learning how to sit with difficult emotions and solving problems directly, because porn becomes emotional anesthesia. That’s why many men on NoFap report benefits that seem unrelated to sex: increased ambition better social confidence more emotional resilience improved discipline stronger routines deeper focus They’re not just abstaining from masturbation . They’re removing a compulsive escape behavior. And once that escape disappears, you’re forced to confront your real life again. That’s uncomfortable at first, but it’s also where growth begins. I noticed something similar after I quit drinking. Alcohol wasn’t just numbing pain. It was numbing my ability to solve problems and enjoy life. When I removed alcohol, I didn’t magically become successful overnight. But I suddenly had no place left to hide from myself. Porn addiction—or any addiction, really—follows the same pattern. That’s why NoFap feels so intense for many men. You aren’t just giving up porn. You’re removing one of the fastest and easiest forms of emotional escape modern technology has ever created. And when that crutch disappears, your mind starts recalibrating itself. That recalibration is where many of the real NoFap benefits begin. NoFap Benefits for Your Brain and Mental Health The first thing many men notice during NoFap isn’t sexual. It’s mental. They start thinking more clearly. Brain fog lifts. Focus improves. Music sounds better. Conversations feel more engaging. Motivation returns. At first, this sounds like internet bro-science, but there’s a reasonable explanation for why this happens. Porn floods the brain with intense novelty and stimulation. Every new image, category, or clip creates another dopamine spike. Over time, your brain adapts to that stimulation by becoming less sensitive to ordinary rewards. This is one reason compulsive porn use can make normal life feel dull by comparison. The problem isn’t dopamine itself. Dopamine is necessary, healthy, and part of the human experience. The problem is overstimulation without effort. Your brain was never designed to experience endless novelty on demand for hours at a time. And when your reward system becomes overloaded, several things can happen: attention becomes fragmented boredom feels unbearable motivation decreases impulses become harder to resist everyday pleasures feel weaker That’s why many men describe compulsive porn use as mentally draining. Not because ejaculation “drains life force.” But because constantly overstimulating the reward system changes what your brain pays attention to. When you quit porn, your brain begins adapting again. This adjustment period is what many people call the “rewiring” process . During the early stages of NoFap, many men report: irritability cravings restlessness anxiety low motivation emotional swings These symptoms are similar to what happens when any compulsive reward behavior is interrupted. Your brain expects stimulation. Then suddenly it’s gone. Over time, many users report the opposite begins happening: improved concentration better emotional control more patience stronger motivation less compulsive thinking increased enjoyment from normal activities The world starts feeling stimulating again without needing constant digital novelty. That’s one of the most commonly reported NoFap benefits. And honestly, it may be one of the most important. NoFap Benefits for Confidence, Discipline, and Self-Respect One of the strangest things about NoFap is how many men report changes in confidence. Not fake confidence. Not loud confidence. Not “alpha male” internet confidence. Real confidence. The kind that comes from finally feeling like you control yourself instead of constantly giving into impulses. That’s an important distinction. Most people think confidence comes from: status money validation attention from women But a huge part of confidence actually comes from self-trust. Can you keep promises to yourself? delay gratification? stay disciplined when nobody is watching? tolerate discomfort without escaping it? Porn quietly weakens that relationship with yourself. Not because porn makes you evil, but because compulsive behavior trains you to prioritize immediate relief over long-term growth. That pattern spreads. You procrastinate more easily. You avoid hard conversations. You seek stimulation instead of purpose. You numb stress instead of confronting it. And deep down, part of you knows it. That’s why compulsive porn use often comes packaged with: shame secrecy low motivation social anxiety lack of direction NoFap interrupts that cycle. Every day you resist compulsive urges, you reinforce something important: “I am capable of controlling myself.” That changes people. Many men report: stronger eye contact less social anxiety more assertiveness better posture improved communication increased willingness to take risks greater emotional stability Some of this may come from reduced shame. Some may come from increased discipline. Some may come from simply feeling proud of yourself again. Pride isn't always a bad thing. A man who feels weak, compulsive, and out of control carries himself differently than a man who feels disciplined and intentional. You can see it in how he talks. How he walks. How he handles pressure. How he responds to discomfort. That’s why many men describe NoFap as more than quitting porn. They describe it as reclaiming agency over their lives. And once that momentum starts building, the effects often spread into everything else: fitness work relationships sleep finances routines ambition Discipline tends to compound. So does self-respect. NoFap Benefits for Sex, Libido, and Relationships One of the biggest reasons men start NoFap is because something feels wrong sexually. For some, it’s erectile dysfunction. For others, it’s delayed ejaculation. Low libido, performance anxiety. escalating fetishes. and/or difficulty becoming aroused by real partners. All of these are problem no man wants to admit that he has, but it gets even worse. Porn begins to affect them more than real intimacy does. That realization is often the wake-up call. Porn trains sexual arousal around: endless novelty constant stimulation voyeurism escalation instant gratification unrealistic scenarios Real sex doesn’t work like that. Real intimacy is slower, messier, and requires emotionally vulnerable. It's not shot from perfect camera angles. When the brain becomes conditioned to hyperstimulating digital sexual content, some men begin struggling to respond normally to real-life experiences. Research has increasingly explored links between compulsive pornography use and sexual dysfunction , particularly in younger men who grew up with unlimited high-speed internet porn available at all times. Now, this doesn’t mean porn affects everyone equally. But for some men, constant overstimulation appears to change sexual expectations, arousal patterns, and reward sensitivity. That’s why many men report major sexual benefits after quitting porn : stronger libido improved erections increased sensitivity more attraction to real partners greater emotional intimacy less performance anxiety reduced dependence on fantasy A lot of men also describe something surprising: They stop seeing women as stimulation first and people second. That matters more than most people realize. Compulsive porn use can distort how attraction works by not only creating exaggerated expectations, but frustrating men when those fantasies aren't realized. Porn encourages endless consumption without emotional connection. Novelty without vulnerability and fantasy without responsibility, but NoFap often reverses that process. Men begin reconnecting sexual desire with: real intimacy emotional presence attraction to actual people touch chemistry connection That’s why many users describe NoFap as a “sexual reset.” Not because sexuality disappears. But because sexuality starts feeling human again instead of algorithmic. And for many men, that becomes one of the most meaningful NoFap benefits of all. The NoFap Timeline: What Men Commonly Experience One reason NoFap becomes so emotionally intense is because recovery rarely happens in a straight line. A lot of men expect instant transformation. They think: “I’ll quit porn and suddenly feel unstoppable.” That usually isn’t what happens. In reality, most people go through stages. There are cravings. Mood swings. Periods of confidence. Periods of doubt. Moments where you feel amazing. Moments where you feel worse than before. That’s normal. When you remove a compulsive source of stimulation, your brain has to adjust to functioning without constant dopamine spikes and instant gratification. For many men, the first week is the hardest. Days 1–7: Cravings and Withdrawal This is usually where urges hit hardest. Your brain is still expecting the same stimulation patterns it’s used to: scrolling novelty fantasy release repeat When that cycle disappears, many men report: irritability anxiety restlessness low motivation trouble focusing intense cravings Some even experience temporary increases in porn thoughts because the brain is actively seeking the reward it expects. This doesn’t mean NoFap is failing. It often means your brain is adjusting. At the same time, some users begin noticing early benefits: small increases in mental clarity reduced guilt better sleep increased awareness of compulsive habits The first stage is less about feeling powerful and more about surviving the adjustment period. Weeks 2–4: Emotional Recalibration This is where things often become psychologically interesting. The constant cravings usually decrease in intensity. But emotions often become stronger. A lot of men realize they were using porn to avoid feelings they didn’t want to confront: loneliness insecurity boredom rejection stress uncertainty Without porn acting as an escape valve, those emotions surface more clearly. That can feel uncomfortable. But it can also be productive. Many users report: improved focus stronger emotional awareness increased motivation more energy for real-world goals better routines greater confidence from staying disciplined This is often the stage where men begin redirecting energy into: lifting weights career goals socializing hobbies therapy spirituality self-improvement NoFap starts becoming less about resisting porn and more about rebuilding life. Days 30–90: Stability and Momentum By this stage, many men report that porn no longer dominates their attention the way it once did. Cravings still happen. But they feel less automatic. Less controlling. Less emotionally overwhelming. This is where many of the most meaningful NoFap benefits tend to appear: sustained focus improved self-control healthier sexual desire stronger routines emotional stability increased self-respect better social confidence Some users also experience what’s known as the “flatline,” a temporary period of low libido or emotional numbness. This stage can feel discouraging. But many people report it passes with time. The important thing to understand is this: NoFap is not about becoming superhuman. It’s about becoming less compulsive. And for many men, that alone changes everything. Are NoFap Benefits Actually Scientific? This is where the internet usually falls apart. One side says: “NoFap is pseudoscience.” The other says: “Semen retention unlocks superhuman powers.” Reality is probably somewhere in the middle. Research specifically on NoFap itself is still limited. Most studies focus on: compulsive pornography use behavioral addiction sexual dysfunction dopamine and reward systems compulsive sexual behavior That distinction matters. There is not strong scientific evidence that abstaining from ejaculation alone gives men magical cognitive or hormonal advantages. But there is growing evidence that compulsive pornography use can negatively affect some people psychologically, sexually, and behaviorally. That’s an important difference. Many NoFap benefits are likely not caused by “saving semen.” They’re more likely caused by: interrupting compulsive behavior reducing overstimulation restoring attention span decreasing shame improving discipline rebuilding self-control reconnecting with real-life rewards In other words: The benefits may come less from mystical biology and more from behavioral recovery. And honestly, that explanation makes far more sense. Think about what happens when a man: stops wasting hours scrolling porn sleeps better exercises consistently feels less ashamed gains confidence from self-discipline becomes less compulsive spends more time pursuing meaningful goals Of course his life improves. That doesn’t require magic. It requires behavioral change. At the same time, it’s important not to exaggerate the science. Some internet claims around NoFap are weak or unsupported: massive testosterone increases instant female attraction supernatural charisma permanent dopamine “damage” becoming biologically superior A lot of this comes from online mythology, not strong evidence. But dismissing the entire movement is also shortsighted. Because clearly, many men are experiencing real positive changes when they quit compulsive porn use. The smarter question is: “Why are these changes happening?” And for many people, the answer has less to do with semen retention and more to do with reclaiming control over attention, behavior, and reward-seeking patterns. The Biggest Mistake Men Make on NoFap A lot of men treat NoFap like a magic pill. They think: “If I just stop watching porn, my entire life will fix itself.” That’s usually where people fail. NoFap by itself does not create a better life. It creates space for one. That’s a huge difference. When you remove compulsive porn use, you suddenly free up: time attention emotional energy motivation mental bandwidth But if you don’t redirect those things somewhere meaningful, your brain will eventually go looking for the old stimulation again. That’s why relapse often happens during: boredom loneliness stress isolation lack of purpose Porn is rarely just about sex. For many men, it’s: distraction escape emotional regulation comfort avoidance If you remove the habit without changing the life around it, the vacuum becomes hard to sustain. This is why the men who succeed long-term with NoFap usually build new systems around themselves. They start: lifting weights sleeping better pursuing goals improving social skills reconnecting with spirituality building routines reducing isolation developing discipline in other areas The real transformation comes from what replaces porn. That’s why so many successful NoFap stories eventually stop being about porn entirely. The conversation shifts toward: fitness purpose relationships confidence ambition self-respect emotional control Porn was never the center of the story. It was the thing standing in the way of it. That’s also why some men become disappointed with NoFap. They quit porn… …but keep: doomscrolling isolating themselves avoiding responsibility chasing easy dopamine neglecting sleep living without direction Then they wonder why nothing changed. NoFap works best when it becomes part of a larger identity shift. Not: “I’m a guy trying not to watch porn.” But: “I’m becoming someone who doesn’t need compulsive escape behaviors anymore.” That mindset changes everything. Because long-term recovery is rarely about white-knuckling urges forever. It’s about building a life you no longer want to escape from. Final Thoughts on NoFap Benefits The internet has turned NoFap into two extremes. One side acts like porn is harmless and anyone who quits it is irrational. The other side talks about semen retention like it unlocks mystical powers. Neither explanation fully captures what’s actually happening. For many men, NoFap works because it forces them to confront something deeper: compulsive behavior emotional escape overstimulation lack of discipline fractured attention disconnection from real life Porn is often just the symptom. The real battle is learning how to tolerate discomfort without constantly escaping into stimulation. That’s why the strongest NoFap benefits are usually not sexual at all. The biggest changes men report are things like: mental clarity emotional control motivation self-respect confidence focus discipline stronger relationships greater purpose Those are not magical powers. They are the side effects of becoming less compulsive and more intentional. And honestly, modern life makes that harder than ever. Your attention is constantly under attack: pornography social media doomscrolling instant gratification endless novelty algorithmic stimulation NoFap matters to many men because it becomes a rebellion against all of that. A decision to stop being controlled by impulses. A decision to reclaim attention. A decision to stop numbing discomfort and start building a life worth being fully awake for. That’s why the movement resonates so deeply. At its core, NoFap is not really about porn. It’s about agency. And for many men, reclaiming that agency changes far more than their sex life.

title: Ocugen Provides Business Update with First Quarter 2026 Financial Results
summary: Conference Call and Webcast Today at 8:30 a.m. ET Positive 12-month data from the OCU410 Phase 2 ArMaDa clinical trial for geographic atrophy (GA) indicates a statistically significant (p
body_text: Conference Call and Webcast Today at 8:30 a.m. ET Positive 12-month data from the OCU410 Phase 2 ArMaDa clinical trial for geographic atrophy (GA) indicates a statistically significant (p<0.05) 31% reduction in lesion size and 27% EZ preservation (correlated to visual function) in optimal dose for Phase 3 About 20% of patients demonstrated no progression of disease and 75% of subjects showed > 30% reduction in Iesion growth compared to control, with a favorable safety and tolerability profile Allows robust registrational Phase 3 trial design, a potential combined U.S./EU trial with 300 subjects, with adaptive design powered at over 95% Trial enrollment complete for OCU400 for retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and OCU410ST for Stargardt disease registration trials, and on target to complete two Biologics License Application (BLA) submissions by 2027 The closing of a private offering of $115 million aggregate principal amount ($130 million if overallotment is exercised) of 6.75% convertible senior notes due 2034, with a conversion premium of 45%, is expected to extend cash runway into 2028, subject to customary closing conditions The Company expects to utilize $32.7 million of net proceeds from the Notes to retire the Avenue debt (12.5% interest rate) MALVERN, Pa., May 05, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ocugen, Inc. (“Ocugen” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: OCGN), a pioneering biotechnology leader in gene therapies for blindness diseases, today reported first quarter 2026 financial results along with a general business update. With the recent offering, the Company is expected to have cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $112.1 million, at closing, which includes the Avenue debt payoff. The Company will use the remaining net proceeds for general corporate purposes and expects to extend cash runway into 2028. The offering is expected to close on May 7, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions and includes an option to retire the debt with a cash payment. If the remaining Janus Henderson warrants are exercised, the Company will receive an additional $15 million in gross proceeds increasing expected cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash to $127.1 million. “In the first few months of 2026, we have completed enrollment of two of our late-stage programs and are diligently working toward initiating our first BLA submission for RP and registration trial for dry AMD later this year,” said Dr. Shankar Musunuri, Chairman, Chief Executive Officer, and Co-Founder of Ocugen. “We are executing well against our plans with the highest productivity per employee rate compared to our peers, adequate cash runway with the recent offering, and key milestone achievement to create long-term value creation for our patients and shareholders.” Enrollment for liMeliGhT, the first and largest gene therapy registrational trial for broad RP patients (N=140), was completed, reflecting strong engagement from investigators and patients. The OCU400 Phase 3 clinical trial includes representation of a wide range of genetic mutations associated with early to advanced stages of clinical and/or genetic diagnosis of RP (over 25 genetic mutations), and patient response is intended to support the gene-agnostic mechanism of action of Ocugen’s novel modifier gene therapy platform. The Company plans to initiate the rolling BLA submission for OCU400 in the third quarter of 2026 and complete the BLA submission by the second quarter of 2027. Manufacturing readiness for OCU400 is well underway and completion of process performance qualification (PPQ) batches remains on track for the second quarter of 2026. Approximately 300,000 people in the U.S. and Europe are living with RP, and OCU400 is intended as a treatment for early to advanced cases of RP, with potential approval in the fourth quarter of 2027. GARDian3 clinical trial enrollment and dosing were completed ahead of schedule. GARDian3 is a multicenter, randomized, masked, pivotal Phase 2/3 confirmatory registration trial designed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of OCU410ST in patients with all mutations of Stargardt disease. The study enrolled 63 subjects diagnosed with Stargardt disease. Subjects randomized to the treatment group received a one-time subretinal injection of OCU410ST in the eye with poorer visual acuity, while the untreated control group did not receive any treatment. The primary endpoint is to evaluate the reduction in atrophic lesion size at 12 months. Key secondary endpoints include improvements in best corrected visual acuity (BCVA) and low luminance visual acuity (LLVA), compared to controls. Observational endpoints include preservation of Ellipsoid Zone (EZ), which correlates to visual function. While demonstrating functional benefit via visual acuity within 12 months can be challenging due to the disease’s natural history, it is believed that preservation of EZ will serve as a meaningful and early indicator of visual function. The interim outcome analysis of 24 subjects at 8 months post-OCU410ST (16 treated and 8 controls) is planned for the third quarter of 2026. Topline results are expected in the second quarter of 2027 with the BLA submission by mid-2027. Interim outcome analysis via adaptive design is typically introduced in pivotal trials to minimize risk. OCU410ST represents a potential first-in-class, one-time modifier gene therapy for all 100,000 patients in the U.S. and Europe with Stargardt disease. Topline 12‑month data from the OCU410 Phase 2 ArMaDa clinical trial for geographic atrophy secondary to dry age-related macular degeneration was announced in March 2026 and demonstrates a statistically significant (p< 0.05) reduction in lesion growth (31%) versus control at 12 months with the optimal dose—medium dose—intended for Phase 3. The data suggest a potential 2X treatment benefit compared to 15% and 22% reductions reported for currently approved therapies at 12 and 24 months, respectively. In the Phase 2 study, the safety and efficacy of OCU410 in patients with GA secondary to dAMD are being assessed. Fifty-one (51) patients aged 50 years and older with GA lesions within the foveal or non-foveal region were randomized 1:1:1 to receive a single subretinal administration of OCU410 at the medium dose, high dose, or no treatment in the control group. The primary endpoint was change in GA lesion size at 12 months, measured in square millimeters by fundus autofluorescence, an FDA-accepted structural endpoint used in recent GA registration trials. Exploratory endpoints included assessment of EZ preservation. The data showed no disease progression in approximately 20% of treated subjects, and 75% of treated subjects demonstrated greater than 30% reduction in lesion growth. The Company plans to initiate the OCU410 Phase 3 registrational trial in the third quarter of 2026 with potential BLA filing by 2028. As a potential one-time treatment for life, OCU410 could eliminate the treatment burden and patient fatigue with up to 40% drop-out rates reported with current approved therapies and provide a one-time solution for the 2-3 million patients in the U.S. and Europe with GA. OCU410 has potential to become a new standard of care for patients across the globe. Executive leadership has participated in significant investor and industry conferences, including the U.S. Department of Commerce 2026 Certified Trade Mission to Singapore; Oppenheimer’s 3rd Annual Innovation on the Island Biotech Summit; and the 2026 Cell & Gene Meeting on the Mediterranean, hosted by the Alliance for Regenerative Medicine. Through these forums, Ocugen reached a wide audience and informed them about the importance of changing the treatment paradigm for blindness diseases by potentially bringing transformative modifier gene therapies to the masses. “We are actively pursuing a variety of business development opportunities to prepare for global commercialization,” said Dr. Musunuri. “Potential commercial partnerships will allow us to effectively provide market access to patients who are in desperate need for rescue from blindness diseases globally while growing shareholder value.” Business Updates Novel Modifier Gene Therapy Platform—Targeting Three BLA Filings in the Next Three Years OCU400 Completed Phase 3 liMeliGhT enrollment (N=140 subjects). Topline Phase 3 data expected in the first quarter of 2027, advancing OCU400 towards potential approval in the fourth quarter of 2027 as a treatment option for early- to late-stage RP. OCU410ST Early completion of enrollment and dosing—less than nine months—in the Phase 2/3 pivotal confirmatory trial (N=63 subjects). Plan to submit the BLA for OCU410ST by mid-2027. OCU410 Announced positive 12-month topline data from the Phase 2 ArMaDa clinical trial. On track to meet with FDA/EMA to align on the Phase 3 study design and initiate Phase 3 by the third quarter of 2026. Other Programs OCU200 Completed Phase 1 clinical trial enrollment in the first quarter of 2026. OCU500 NIAID intends to initiate the OCU500 Phase 1 clinical trial in the second quarter of 2026. The Company’s cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash totaled $32.2 million as of March 31, 2026, compared to $18.9 million as of December 31, 2025. With the recent offering, the Company is expected to have cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash of $112.1 million, at closing, which includes the Avenue debt payoff. summary: SINGAPORE, May 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Antalpha Platform Holding Company (NASDAQ: ANTA) ("Antalpha" or the "Company") today announced its unaudited financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026. “Antalpha continued to demonstrate the resilience and scalability of its platform in
body_text: Antalpha Reports First Quarter 2026 Results May 19, 2026 PDF Version SINGAPORE, May 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Antalpha Platform Holding Company (NASDAQ: ANTA) ("Antalpha" or the "Company") today announced its unaudited financial results for the first quarter ended March 31, 2026. “Antalpha continued to demonstrate the resilience and scalability of its platform in the first quarter, with sustained revenue growth and profitability through a more challenging market environment,” said Paul Liang, Chief Financial Officer of Antalpha. “What stood out in the first quarter of 2026 was how the two distinct sides of Antalpha's platform worked together harmoniously. Our tokenized gold upside captured the constructive move in gold prices, and our lending portfolio, conservatively collateralized and still with no loss of principal to date, continued to reflect the risk discipline that has long defined our business.” “Our central strategy is to build a comprehensive digital asset infrastructure platform over time, which may include expanding into adjacent opportunities that leverage our core strengths,” continued Mr. Liang. “As our most recent technology platform initiative, we are excited to have launched our Web3 AI agent in beta, bringing on-chain execution, data analytics, and crypto investment tools directly to end users, built on the deep Web3 expertise we have accumulated over our years specializing in this ecosystem. We are also advancing our tokenized gold strategy, which is beginning to generate meaningful yield. We believe these initiatives best position Antalpha to grow meaningfully across multiple dimensions of the digital asset ecosystem.” First Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights For the three Months Ended March 31, (In US$1 millions, unaudited) 2025 2026 YOY Total Revenue $13.6 $20.7 52 % Net income attributable to Antalpha* $1.5 $2.7 85 % Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)** $2.5 $13.3 435% Adjusted EBITDA Margin (non-GAAP)* 18 % 64 % 46 pts As of March 31, (In US$1 millions, unaudited) 2025 2026 YOY Supply Chain TVL $578 $434 -25% Margin Loan TVL*** $1,189 $1,280 8% Total Value of Loans (TVL) Facilitated $1,767 $1,714 -3% * The Company's Q1 2026 results reflect the consolidated results of the Company and Aurelion (NASDAQ: AURE) following the acquisition of a controlling interest in Aurelion on October 10, 2025, whereas Q1 2025 results represent the Company's standalone results. ** Please see “Non-GAAP Measures” and “Reconciliations of non-GAAP financial measures to the nearest comparable GAAP measures” below for further information on non-GAAP numbers. *** Antalpha earns technology platform fees on margin loans, which it acts as an agent and assumes no principal credit exposure. First Quarter 2026 Performance Highlights Resilient Revenue Growth Total revenue was $20.7 million, an increase of 52% year-over-year (“YOY”), reflecting continued platform scale despite a challenging market backdrop. High-Quality Loan Book Maintained disciplined collateral coverage and risk management standards across the platform. As of March 31, 2026: Total value of loans (“TVL”) per client increased 36% YOY, indicating deeper client relationships and higher engagement. TVL was $1.7 billion, a 3% decrease YOY, reflecting more measured deployment activity in a weaker Bitcoin price environment and substantial loan repayments by certain large borrowers in early 2026. Improved Lending Economics Net fee margin (“NFM”) increased 21 basis points YOY, demonstrating the platform's continued pricing power and product mix management. The improvement was led by stronger margin loan take rates, while supply chain loan margins remained resilient against a backdrop of evolving product mix. Operating Expenses Operating expenses excluding unrealized gain on crypto assets were $25.0 million, up 102% YOY, including funding costs of $10.4 million and approximately $3.3 million of one-time restructuring charges and $1.3 million non-cash share-based compensation combined. Non-GAAP operating expenses, which exclude unrealized gain on crypto assets, one-time and non-cash items, were $20.4 million. Measured Profitability Operating income was $6.6 million, representing an operating margin of 32%, primarily reflecting $10.9 million in unrealized fair value gains on XAUt holdings by Aurelion. Non-GAAP operating income, which excludes one-time and non-cash items of $4.6 million, was $11.2 million, representing a non-GAAP operating margin of 54%. Net income attributable to Antalpha was $2.7 million, compared to $1.5 million in the prior-year period. Prior-year figures reflect Antalpha standalone results, as consolidation of Aurelion began in Q4 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.3 million, including approximately $12.9 million in unrealized gains related to XAUt holdings. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 64%, compared to 18% in the prior-year period. Scaling Tokenized Gold Antalpha continued to methodically build its tokenized gold strategy, with a focus on enhancing utility and yield generation. In April, the Company began deploying assets into yield-generating protocols, marking a transition toward more productive use of tokenized gold holdings. Strategic Initiative: Web3 AI -- Building Additional Growth Curve As a natural extension of its technology platform, Antalpha has begun developing a Web3 AI agent, a new product designed to enable users to interact with blockchain networks, access on-chain data, and execute crypto-related tasks through natural language. The initiative builds directly on the Company's established position at the intersection of crypto financing, blockchain data, and compute infrastructure, extending these capabilities into an adjacent opportunity. The Company's deep Web3 domain expertise and existing client relationships within the Bitcoin mining ecosystem provide a natural and differentiated foundation for this development, and Antalpha is excited about its potential. In May 2026, the Company launched an early-stage version of the product in beta, with initial market testing underway. The Company is currently focused on product development and market validation. Financial impact—from both a revenue and expense perspective—is not expected to be material in the near term. Further updates will be provided as the initiative progresses. Outlook Antalpha expects Q2 2026 revenue between $11 million and $13 million. The Company’s guidance assumes continued demand for crypto-collateralized financing, with market conditions remaining dynamic but broadly consistent with recent trends. This forecast reflects Antalpha’s current preliminary view, which is subject to substantial risks and uncertainties. The Company is not obliged to update any forward-looking statements, except as required by law. To attend, please register in advance at: https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BIfb7cbcb3ef3e4019a79ca07ecd069108 . Upon registration, you will receive a calendar invite email that includes dial-in number, passcode, and your unique access PIN. A live webcast can be accessed at https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/4jef7vmv . A replay of the call will also be available on the Company’s investor relations website at https://ir.antalpha.com .
